![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134323/assets/deff964a1833339681fc38b30e32ebd3081e7ba1c4b5aabd0f4998f60a2aa78c.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le v\le 1,\,\frac{v-1}{2}\le u\le \frac{1-v}{2}\}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134323/assets/daefc9e14775a955e5210f965e474c06bc7cac1df9306941b73190cc8bf62219.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-3,-2),(-1,2),$ and $(0,2).$ 

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134323/assets/94a2a90dae43d1edb1f0154a8c7ac60b8c35352fd72d5193014b9bba204d192f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.
